summary: A putative class action filed in Minnesota alleges that UnitedHealthcare and naviHealth used the nH Predict care-management model to curtail Medicare Advantage post-acute coverage for older patients before their treating clinicians considered them ready for discharge. The complaint describes nH Predict as generating expected care durations and alleges that employees were pressured to keep skilled-nursing stays close to those projections. Named plaintiffs alleged that coverage was terminated despite treating-clinician objections, leaving some families to pay substantial costs or forgo further care. In February 2025, a federal judge allowed breach-of-contract and implied-covenant claims to proceed while dismissing several other claims; the surviving contract theory turns on whether UnitedHealthcare complied with plan language stating that clinical staff and physicians make coverage decisions when plaintiffs allege AI was used instead. As of March 2026, that merits question remained unresolved and in discovery.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full review of all 74 current Failure Classes retains VIGIL-FC-000046 Inferential Evidence–Authority Separation as the primary provisional mapping and adds VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Routing as a secondary provisional mapping, both at medium confidence. The complaint alleges that nH Predict’s expected care duration became practically determinative of individual post-acute coverage despite treating-clinician objections, satisfying the evidence-to-authority mechanism if proved. Separately, UnitedHealthcare’s evidence-of-coverage documents stated that clinical services staff and physicians make care decisions, while the surviving contract theory and later discovery orders frame whether nH Predict displaced individualized physician decision-making as a live merits question. That supports a distinct alleged required-route bypass. VIGIL-FC-000016 Required Verification Completion is not established because no separate required verification step is shown to have been omitted and then represented as completed. VIGIL-FC-000038 Required Control Activation is not established because the disputed mechanism is route substitution rather than a defined trigger whose protective control failed to activate. VIGIL-FC-000062 Epistemic Reliance Calibration is not added because the more specific mechanism is promotion of a predictive evidentiary state into authority, not merely use of an insufficiently assured artefact. The mappings remain provisional because the court has not adjudicated that nH Predict actually dictated the named plaintiffs’ denials.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The filed complaint is primary evidence of the plaintiffs’ allegations. It alleges that nH Predict generated patient-specific expected lengths of post-acute care, that those estimates became rigid practical cutoffs, and that staff who deviated from the model could be disciplined. For Gene Lokken, the complaint alleges coverage was terminated while physical-therapy records still described significant weakness, that repeated appeals failed, and that his family paid roughly $12,000–$14,000 per month for continued skilled-nursing care. Those assertions remain contested. The February 2025 federal order supplies a stronger procedural and governance boundary: the court allowed contract claims to proceed because UnitedHealthcare’s evidence-of-coverage documents stated that clinical services staff and physicians make care decisions, making compliance with that representation a live contractual question when plaintiffs allege AI was used. A September 2025 order described the merits issue as whether coverage decisions were made using nH Predict instead of individualized physician-medical-director decisions. A March 2026 discovery order again treated whether nH Predict was used to make coverage determinations as unresolved, merits-based, and directly relevant to discovery. The Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations separately reported that UnitedHealthcare’s post-acute prior-authorization denial rate rose from 10.9% in 2020 to 22.7% in 2022 as automated processes expanded. None of those later sources adjudicates the named plaintiffs’ individual causation or establishes that every denial was dictated by nH Predict.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evidence supports a provisional two-part governance interpretation. First, the complaint describes a population-derived prediction being treated as practically determinative of an individual patient’s post-acute coverage despite contrary clinical information; if established, that is an evidence-to-authority conversion rather than ordinary decision support. Second, the surviving contract claims and later discovery orders identify a distinct route question: whether a process represented as requiring clinical staff and physician decision-making was allegedly displaced by nH Predict. Both mechanisms remain allegation-bounded because the court has not determined that nH Predict actually dictated the named plaintiffs’ coverage decisions. The record therefore preserves the mappings at medium confidence rather than treating the litigation posture as proof of liability or of every pleaded factual claim.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence separates two governance questions that should not be collapsed. A predictive care-duration estimate may be a legitimate decision-support input, but it must not become individual entitlement authority beyond what the estimate can establish. Separately, where the governing coverage process represents consequential decisions as being made by clinical staff and physicians, an alternate automated pathway must not displace that required review route without an authorised equivalent. The litigation remains important precisely because those alleged mechanisms are testable without assuming the plaintiffs have already proved them.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All eleven VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1 dimensions were reopened against the complaint and later court record. Alleged worsening injury or death is not independently attributed to the disputed decision pathway strongly enough for a separate physical-health band.
